fact: In N7 context the one lexical collision is decided by whether the line has trailing text, not by the source kind alone. `Artifact manifest: m.json, sha256 H, 5 bytes.` binds `m.json` (N7 delimiter), but the same line with a permitted suffix (`... 5 bytes. note`) fails the N7 full-match, falls through to pass03 FIELD_RE and binds `m.json,` with no finding. So on an N7 page the same declaration names two different files depending on a free-text tail. CONTRACT says 'Nothing else collides'; this near-collision is not listed.
evidence: workers/A/probes/probe_parse.py (output probe_parse.out.json) case C4_collision_with_suffix vs C5_collision_plain
labs/n7-intake-compat-pass02/tests/test_n7v2.py lines 126-130: author P6 tests trailing text only on a Returned line, not on the N7 manifest line, so C4 is not covered
method: read + probe. Probe ran these original functions, extracted by AST from the frozen files without running their module top level: pass02 suffix_ok; pass03 accept_field and parse_pointer; n7compat2 make_parser (parser built with kind_fn fixed to N7NN and to N5NN); proposal parse_n7.
impact: On an N7 page a manifest declared with a trailing note resolves to a comma filename that (per CONTRACT lines 37-39) does not exist, so measurement becomes missing silently, or, if such a file exists, binds a different file than the author meant. The meaning flip is invisible in findings.
recommendation: Decide explicitly: either make the N7 manifest form accept the same suffix rule as pass03 (suffix_ok) so the delimiter reading is stable, or emit a finding when an N7-context FIELD_RE match has a path ending in ',' that would have matched the N7 form without its tail. Add C4 as a contract case.
label: verified

fact: A line that the N7 grammar refuses does not count toward ambiguity. A `Returned:` line refused as attribution-not-descriptive, followed by a `Submission:` line naming a different file and hash, leaves Submission bound to the second line with state 'parsed'. Likewise a refused collision-with-label-suffix manifest line followed by a valid N7 manifest binds the valid one.
method: read + probe. Probe ran these original functions, extracted by AST from the frozen files without running their module top level: pass02 suffix_ok; pass03 accept_field and parse_pointer; n7compat2 make_parser (parser built with kind_fn fixed to N7NN and to N5NN); proposal parse_n7.
impact: Two contradictory Submission declarations can coexist on an N7 page and one wins silently (only an attribution-not-descriptive / unparsed-return-line finding is left). This mirrors pass03's handling of unparsed lines, so it is inherited, but N7 adds a new refusal class (attribution) that feeds the same hole.
recommendation: Either treat a refused labelled line as occupying its field (mark the field ambiguous), or state in CONTRACT that refused lines never affect binding. Prime decision; not a defect if intended.
label: verified

fact: The 'descriptive only' attribution check is narrow: it looks only for a lowercase 64-hex run and case-sensitive label words. An attribution with an uppercase 64-hex run (`copy of AAAA...`), a lowercase label word (`see submission: other.md`), or only a space (`( )`) is accepted and binds the Submission.
evidence: workers/A/probes/probe_parse.py (output probe_parse.out.json) cases C2, C3, C7
method: read + probe. Probe ran these original functions, extracted by AST from the frozen files without running their module top level: pass02 suffix_ok; pass03 accept_field and parse_pointer; n7compat2 make_parser (parser built with kind_fn fixed to N7NN and to N5NN); proposal parse_n7.
impact: attribution_text is not stored (CONTRACT line 53), so impact is limited to a weaker-than-stated guard; no wrong file is bound by this alone.
recommendation: If the guard matters, match hex case-insensitively, label words case-insensitively, and require at least one non-space character. Otherwise soften the CONTRACT wording.
label: verified

fact: The kind wrapper calls address_of(source, pass_id) before delegating, i.e. before pass02 build_intake runs its pin_file checks. For an invalid source or pass, the refusal now comes from the wrapper's address_of call ahead of any pin refusal; in unpatched pass03 the pin checks run first. address_of is also evaluated twice per intake.
method: read only (no run; pass02 build_intake cannot run here without the D: tree)
impact: Only the order/message of refusals can differ, and only when both the source/pass and a pin are bad. address_of is pure (regex + dict), so the double call has no state effect. Not covered by the N5 replay, which used a valid source.
recommendation: Note as accepted, or move the KIND set after pin checks (e.g. derive kind inside a guarded try that falls back to None on Refusal and lets pass02 refuse in its own order).
label: inferred

fact: The stored intake record does not keep which grammar form bound a field. measure_declared keeps only path/sha256/bytes (rows: bytes, declared_bytes, declared_path, declared_sha256, path, role, root, sha256); attribution_text and declared_form exist only in the transient parsed pointer. The record does keep 'kind', so the grammar can be re-derived, but not whether a manifest was read via the N7 delimiter or the pass03 form (see A-01).
impact: An auditor reading the stored record cannot tell from the record alone which reading was applied to an N7 manifest line; must re-parse the page bytes.
recommendation: If evidence-per-pass matters, consider recording declared_form in findings (not rows) so the record schema stays unchanged.
label: verified (by read)
